summary: Reuse decisions for each analyzed repository: CAN_LIFT, MUST_REBUILD, or HYBRID

decision_criteria.CAN_LIFT: License permits use, code quality good, directly applicable, dependencies compatible
decision_criteria.MUST_REBUILD: Incompatible license, code quality issues, tightly coupled to proprietary systems, or fundamental mismatch
decision_criteria.HYBRID: License permits use but strategic reasons to rebuild (e.g., different tech stack, simplification needed, EOL status)

repositories.rationale: Legally can lift entire codebase. Technically, architecture excellent but Java/Eclipse ecosystem not ideal for Python project. ADAPT: Use architectural patterns (Template Method, Plugin Architecture) but reimplement in Python with Jinja2 templates.
Legally can lift but UML already has metamodel defined by OMG. No need for new DSL. Value is studying type system design, validation architecture, and expression language patterns.
what_to_rebuild: Not applicable - UML metamodel already defined
repositories.dependencies_review: Eclipse Xtext, EMF - heavy dependencies, not needed if not building DSL

repositories.rationale: Legally clear. Angular 14 outdated, CDM-specific. Adapt schema-driven UI generation pattern and tree-based object builder for UML. Rebuild with modern stack (React 18, TypeScript 5).
repositories.dependencies_review: Angular, RxJS, Material Design - all permissive licenses

repositories.rationale: Starter code is Apache 2.0 and liftable. CDM dependency uses Community Spec License - can implement spec freely. Minimal code, mainly useful for patterns (Maven config, test data loading). Study and adapt patterns rather than lift code.
repositories.dependencies_review: JUnit, Jackson - permissive. CDM - Community Spec (implementation freedom)

repositories.rationale: Can freely implement specification. Code is Apache 2.0. Financial domain specific, so direct lift inappropriate. HYBRID: Adopt architectural patterns (event model, qualification functions, type system), study governance, avoid financial-specific implementations.
what_to_rebuild: Financial domain models → UML domain (if building UML-specific patterns)
repositories.dependencies_review: Rosetta DSL (Apache 2.0), various Apache 2.0 libraries - all compatible

repositories.rationale: Legally can lift. ARCHIVED (EOL Nov 2025) creates practical concerns. Very high complexity. HYBRID: Study PVM abstraction, Command pattern, State machine, Model API. Adapt specific components. Avoid wholesale adoption due to EOL status and complexity.
what_to_lift: State machine with explicit state tracking
what_to_rebuild: PVM → Simpler execution model for UML
Complex enterprise features → Focused UML features
repositories.dependencies_review: MyBatis, Joda-Time, JUEL - all permissive but some outdated

repositories.rationale: Legally clear. ARCHIVED but stable library. Excellent metamodel implementation patterns. ADAPT: Type Object pattern, fluent builders, XML serialization for UML XMI. Consider code generation for UML's larger scale (700+ metaclasses vs BPMN's 200).
what_to_lift: Fluent builder pattern with recursive generics
what_to_rebuild: Manual implementation → Code generation for UML scale

repositories.rationale: Legally can lift. ACTIVE development (advantage over Camunda). High complexity. HYBRID: Adopt service-oriented API, command pattern, Spring Boot integration. Adapt agenda-based execution, execution tree model. Study but simplify persistence, avoid complex enterprise features.
what_to_rebuild: Workflow execution → UML behavioral diagram execution
Complex enterprise features → Focused UML features
repositories.dependencies_review: MyBatis, Spring, Groovy, Drools - all Apache 2.0 or compatible

primary_obstacles: Scale differences (BPMN 200 types vs UML 700 metaclasses)
Domain specificity (Financial CDM vs general UML)
summary.recommended_approach: Adopt architectural patterns, adapt implementations to Python ecosystem, study complex components for insights, avoid wholesale code lifting due to tech stack differences.

components: Type Object metamodel pattern (from Camunda BPMN model)
Command pattern with interceptors (from both engines)
State machine implementation (from Camunda PVM insights)
Fluent builders for model construction (from BPMN models)

archived_repositories.mitigation: Study patterns only, do not depend on libraries. Flowable actively maintained as alternative reference.

tech_stack_differences.risk: Java patterns may not translate cleanly to Python
tech_stack_differences.mitigation: Proof-of-concept implementations for critical patterns. Use Python-idiomatic approaches (Pydantic, type hints, protocols).

complexity.risk: Workflow engines very complex, may over-engineer UML tool
complexity.mitigation: Start simple, add complexity only when needed. Focus on UML-specific requirements, avoid enterprise workflow features.

scale.mitigation: Use code generation for metamodel implementation. Manual approach works for BPMN but won't scale to UML.
